 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C filed on behalf of applicant for grant of bail,
pending trial.
The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.424/2022 o f Police Station Kolar Road, District Bhopal for commission of offence punishable under Section 376, 376(2)(n), 342, 506 of IPC.
He is in detention since 18.5.2022.

As per prosecution story on 17.5.2022, 55 years old sister-in-law of the present applicant lodged an FIR alleging that her younger brother-in-law along with his wife and children lives on the another side of road of her house.
In the month of December, he came and asked to cook the food.

At this,
she went to his house at around 7 P.M., when she was cooking vegetable, applicant committed rape upon her by raising the sound of TV.

She had informed her husband about the incident but did not Ramesh Tanwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3586883/
1 lodge FIR.

sentences.text: In the meantime, present applicant left for Rajasthan.
On 17.5.2022 at around 2 P.M. he again asked her to come at his home and raped her.
She narrated the entire story to her husband and lodged FIR.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated as there is some property dispute in the family and due to that, he has been falsely implicated.
No FIR was lodged for the alleged incident which took place in the month of December.
Entire story is concocted and baseless.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant be released on bail, pending the trial.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the detention period of the applicant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicant - Ramesh Tanwar be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Ramesh Tanwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3586883/
